source: FICTIONAL desktop-PC maintenance simulation. Illustrative only - not real maintenance advice. Hardware facts to be validated against an equipment source before the main study.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU rocker switch at the rear of the case to O (off).
steps.explanation: The switch isolates mains power from the motherboard. The board still carries standby voltage while the switch is on, so nothing is touched before this.

steps.instruction: Remove the thumbscrew at the bottom-right corner of the side panel.
steps.explanation: The thumbscrew is the only fastener holding the panel. Loosening it by hand avoids tools scratching the paint.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel off to open the case.
steps.explanation: The panel rides on slots along the case edge. Sliding it back first, then lifting, avoids bending the sheet metal.

steps.instruction: Touch the bare metal of the case to discharge static.
steps.explanation: Static electricity from your body can destroy memory chips without any visible spark. Touching bare case metal equalises the charge.

steps.instruction: Open the top retention clip of the RAM slot.
steps.explanation: The clip is a plastic lever that locks the module in place. Opening it releases the top of the module.

steps.instruction: Open the bottom retention clip of the RAM slot.
steps.explanation: Both clips must be open before the module can come out. Forcing it with a clip closed breaks the clip or the slot.

steps.instruction: Pull the RAM module straight up and out of the slot.
steps.explanation: Pulling straight up keeps the gold contacts aligned. Wiggling or pulling at an angle bends the contacts in the slot.

steps.instruction: Press the replacement module into the slot until both clips snap closed.
steps.explanation: The module only fits one way because of the keyed notch. Even pressure until the clips click means the contacts are fully seated.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel back on until it clicks home.
steps.explanation: Closing the case before power is restored keeps dust out and the airflow path intact.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU power switch back to I (on).
steps.explanation: Power is restored only after every part is secured, so the memory controller can retrain during startup.

hazard.message: STATIC WARNING: charge detected on your wrist. Discharge on the case metal before touching the module!
